headline: 860 die as measles outbreak toll rises in Bangladesh
summary: Six more patients died within 24 hours, bringing the total number of confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths this year to 860.
details: Six more patients died with measles-like symptoms in 24 hours, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS). This brings the country's combined tally of confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths to 860 this year.
The latest fatalities were all suspected measles deaths. This has increased the number of suspected deaths to 764, while laboratory-confirmed deaths remain at 96.

Additionally, 85 new confirmed measles cases were recorded, bringing the total number of laboratory-confirmed infections to 16,740.
Since March 15 this year, 115,879 patients with suspected measles have been hospitalised across the country. Of these, 111,587 patients have recovered, according to DGHS data.
caption:
860 deaths and over 133,000 suspected cases. The measles outbreak in Bangladesh is escalating.

Six more patients died with measles-like symptoms in 24 hours, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS). This brings the country's combined tally of confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths to 860 this year.

The latest fatalities were all suspected measles deaths. This has increased the number of suspected deaths to 764, while laboratory-confirmed deaths remain at 96.

A total of 733 new suspected measles cases were reported in the last 24 hours, bringing the cumulative number of suspected cases nationwide to 133,638.

Additionally, 85 new confirmed measles cases were recorded, bringing the total number of laboratory-confirmed infections to 16,740.

Since March 15 this year, 115,879 patients with suspected measles have been hospitalised across the country. Of these, 111,587 patients have recovered, according to DGHS data.

headline_marked: Death penalty law leads [[UN to withhold witness identities]] in July uprising case
headline: Death penalty law leads UN to withhold witness identities in July uprising case
summary: The UN has declined to share the identities of eyewitnesses from its July uprising report due to the death penalty provision in Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal law.
details: The United Nations has withheld the identities of eyewitnesses mentioned in its fact-finding report on human rights violations during the July 2024 uprising. This information was revealed by prosecutor Gazi M.H. Tamim before the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) on Thursday.
caption:
The UN is refusing to share witness names for the July uprising investigation because of Bangladesh's death penalty laws.

The United Nations has withheld the identities of eyewitnesses mentioned in its fact-finding report on human rights violations during the July 2024 uprising. This information was revealed by prosecutor Gazi M.H. Tamim before the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) on Thursday.
